> **What you can defend when you leave.** Prove that someone who is not you can obtain your result from your materials.

## What this station produces

An independent cold-run record and a reusable research package.

This is a **versioned checkpoint**, not a pass. You date it, number it, and
attach the reason for the version. When later evidence changes it, you write
the next version rather than editing the last one, because the sequence of
changes is itself part of your research record.

- [Ch. 34 — Replication and Reproduction](https://davi-moreira.github.io/2026F_evidence_driven_research_purdue_HONR464/book/part6-after-conference/32-replication-and-reproduction.html)
- [Ch. 36 — Open and Reusable Research Packages](https://davi-moreira.github.io/2026F_evidence_driven_research_purdue_HONR464/book/part6-after-conference/34-open-and-reusable-research-packages.html)

Read these before you work the station. The station is where you do the thing
the lessons describe, on your own project.

## The practice

1. Run your own package cold, from a clean environment, following only your written instructions.
2. Have someone else run it without your help, and log every place they had to ask you a question.
3. Fix what the cold run exposed; every question they asked is a missing line in your documentation.
4. Assemble the package: data or its access route, code, environment, documentation, and licence.

## The four rails, here

Four concerns cross every station in this book. At this station they take
these specific forms.

- **Ethics, permissions, and data exposure.** What can be shared is set by your permissions, and the package says so explicitly.
- **Evidence, provenance, and reproducibility.** Reproduction is the evidence rail's final test.
- **AI activity, verification, and human decisions.** An assistant can generate documentation; only a cold human run can validate it.
- **Uncertainty, claim boundary, and revision history.** Reproduce the uncertainty statement, not only the point estimate.

## What sends you back

A failed cold run is a finding about your work, and it precedes any release.

## How this checkpoint is assessed

Each row scores **0**, **1**, or **2**. **10 points total.**

| # | Criterion | 0 | 1 | 2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The station's artifact exists in full, specific to your own project | absent, or generic text that would fit any project | present but incomplete, or specific in some parts and generic in others | complete and unmistakably about your project |
| 2 | The checkpoint is written as a dated, numbered version with its reason | no version, or a version with no reason given | versioned, but the reason is decorative rather than an account of what changed | versioned with a reason a reader could use to reconstruct your thinking |
| 3 | Every judgment in the artifact is defended by you, not asserted by a tool | conclusions appear with no reasoning, or reproduce a tool's wording | reasoning present but thin where the decision was hardest | each judgment carries a reason you could defend under questioning |
| 4 | The four rails are carried in this station's specific form | one or more rails absent where this station required them | all rails present but one is nominal | every rail addressed in the form this station requires |
| 5 | The station's own product is present and defensible: An independent cold-run record and a reusable research package | the station's own product is missing | present but would not survive a careful question | present and defensible as stated |

::: {.callout-important title="Blocking gate"}
No work at or after Station 4 proceeds past a not-authorized determination. This is not scored and cannot be averaged away.
:::
